metadata.title: TIMSS 1999 Database User Guide – Supplement 3: Variables Derived from the Student, Teacher and School Questionnaires
metadata.venue: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement) / International Study Center (ISC)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a TIMSS 1999 database user guide supplement describing how derived background variables (student, teacher, and school questionnaire indices) are computed for use in secondary analyses and in the TIMSS 1999 international reports. It does not provide an analysis sample, estimation model, or any explicit instruction about applying student/sampling weights or replicate weights to produce statistical estimates. For users conducting secondary analyses, the appropriate complex survey design weights and replicate weights (if available in the TIMSS 1999 international database) should be applied according to the main TIMSS 1999 database user guide; this supplement focuses on variable construction and missing rules rather than estimation. Because no empirical modeling is performed here, weight usage is not specified at the supplement level.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this supplement is documentation for derived questionnaire variables and computation rules, not an empirical study predicting cognitive achievement scores from PV-based outcomes. Missing-data handling is described only as variable-specific missing rules for derived indices (e.g., when component items are missing), but the supplement does not report an analysis-level missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation) for any statistical model. Therefore, missing_data_handling is set to not_reported at the paper level because no modeling workflow is evaluated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic student sample is defined in this supplement. Instead, it documents how derived variables are computed from questionnaire source variables, including country-specific inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., only countries administering general vs separate science forms; only countries reporting certain teacher course types via ITCOURSE codes) and variable-specific missing rules (e.g., index computed only when enough component variables are present; otherwise coded as missing).

data.outcome_summary: This supplement is not an empirical ML or statistical results paper; it is a technical documentation for TIMSS 1999 derived background variables. It explains that derived student variables (e.g., indices of self-concept and positive attitudes in science/mathematics), teacher variables (e.g., instructional time allocations, homework emphasis, confidence in preparation), and school variables (e.g., instructional hours, access to internet, attendance/discipline indices) are computed from specific questionnaire source items. It also documents missing rules and country adaptations, including how general/integrated vs separate science questionnaire versions are handled and how teacher panels are filtered using ITCOURSE codes. Finally, it provides computation rules behind selected international-report exhibits where the derived variables are not directly included in the database. As a result, there are no model performance metrics or causal/predictive effects to interpret for policy; the main contribution is reproducibility of variable construction for secondary analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a database user guide supplement rather than an empirical research article. It does not report an analytic sample size, country-level Ns, or any predictive/causal modeling results, and it does not train or evaluate machine learning models. Consequently, fields such as total_students, countries with per-country sample sizes, ML techniques, and main findings are not applicable to extract from the provided text.
